cards.title: Turning a 22-year-old Postgres type-confusion primitive into RCE

glossary.Cargo: Rust’s tool for building Rust projects.
glossary.minimum-publish-age: A rule that makes Cargo wait a set amount of time after a package version appears before using it.
glossary.dependency cooldowns: A way to wait before using newly published package versions, giving problems time to be spotted.
glossary.never type: A type for code that never reaches a normal result because it exits or keeps running instead.
glossary.supply-chain attack: An attack that slips harmful code into software people get through a tool or package they trust.
glossary.digitizing: Turning artwork into instructions for an embroidery machine, including how the stitches should go.
glossary.PES/DST: File types used to store embroidery designs so machines can read them.
glossary.SVG: Scalable Vector Graphics: a picture format that stays sharp when resized.
glossary.API: Application Programming Interface: a way for one program to ask another for information or actions.
glossary.reverse engineering: Figuring out how a program works by examining the program itself.
glossary.LLM: Large Language Model: an AI trained on lots of writing so it can take written questions and produce written answers.
glossary.ITAR: International Traffic in Arms Regulations: US rules that restrict sharing certain military-related technology.
glossary.fiduciary duty: A legal responsibility to make decisions in the interests of a company or the people it represents.
glossary.interim CEO: A temporary chief executive who runs a company until a longer-term choice is made.
glossary.model router: A tool that picks which AI model handles a task.
glossary.quota: The amount of usage a service allows before it limits what you can do.
glossary.SDK: Software Development Kit: tools a company provides so people can make apps for its device.
glossary.agent: An AI system that can take steps and use tools to get a task done, not just answer questions.
glossary.long-horizon task: A job that takes many steps or keeps running over a longer period.
glossary.dwarf planet: A nearly round object orbiting a star that hasn't cleared similar-sized debris from its path.
glossary.infrared light: Light we can't see that lets astronomers measure heat coming from an object.
glossary.photographic plates: Flat sheets used to record photographs before modern digital cameras.
glossary.GPU: Graphics Processing Unit: the chip part that draws images and video.
glossary.model weights: The learned settings inside an AI that shape how it responds.
glossary.seed: The starting number that helps determine what numbers a random-number generator produces.
glossary.SM: Streaming Multiprocessor: one of a GPU’s processing units that handles calculations.
glossary.hardware fingerprint: A pattern in a model’s starting numbers that can hint at which chip created them.
glossary.distillation: Training a smaller AI to imitate the answers of a larger one.
glossary.export controls: Rules that limit where a company can sell certain goods, often for security reasons.
glossary.TRT: Testosterone replacement therapy: medical treatment that provides testosterone to someone whose body has too little.
glossary.LLMs: Large language models: computer programs trained on lots of writing that can produce text.
glossary.abstractions: Simpler ways to organize code so you can work with an idea without handling every detail.
glossary.IPC: Inter-process communication: a way for separate programs on one computer to exchange information.
glossary.L3 cache: A processor's shared stash of data, meant to save trips to main memory.
glossary.SMT: Simultaneous multithreading: a way for one processor core to work on more than one stream of instructions at a time.
glossary.VNNI: Vector Neural Network Instructions: special processor commands used for number-heavy tasks such as the AI and video work mentioned here.
glossary.parameters: Learned values inside a model that shape the answers it gives.
glossary.inference: When an AI uses what it learned to answer or act, instead of being trained.
glossary.tokens/s: Tokens per second: a rough measure of how quickly a model produces text.
glossary.open weights: The model's learned settings are available for people to download and run themselves.
glossary.server models: AI models that run on a provider's computers rather than directly on your device.
glossary.Swift API: A way for an app written in Swift to use features from another piece of software.
glossary.Dynamic Profiles: Different saved setups an app can switch between, each choosing its AI model, available tools, and instructions.
glossary.Evaluations framework: A way to test whether an AI feature still works when the request or setup changes.
glossary.wholesale electricity prices: The prices utilities pay for electricity before it is delivered to homes.
glossary.energy burden: How much of a household's income goes to paying for energy.
glossary.baseload generation: Power supply meant to run steadily, rather than only when demand peaks.
glossary.transmission infrastructure: The lines and equipment that carry electricity from where it is made to where it is used.
glossary.type confusion: When a program treats data as one kind of thing even though it was created as another.
glossary.composite type: A database value made up of named fields, like a row with several columns.
glossary.prepared statement: A query the database works out first and can run later with values supplied separately.
glossary.bytea: PostgreSQL’s type for storing bytes that aren’t necessarily readable text.
glossary.RCE: Remote Code Execution: a flaw that lets an attacker make a computer run their commands from somewhere else.
glossary.Datum: A PostgreSQL container for a value, which may hold the value itself or refer to where it is stored.
glossary.letter rogatory: A formal request asking another country’s authorities to help gather evidence in a legal case.
glossary.subpoena: A legal order telling someone to provide records or appear in court.
glossary.data centers: Large buildings full of computers that store or process information.
glossary.AUv3: Audio Unit version 3: Apple's way for music-making add-ons to run inside compatible apps.
glossary.VST: Virtual Studio Technology: a format for add-ons that give music software new instruments or effects.
glossary.MIDI: Musical Instrument Digital Interface: a way for music software and instruments to share notes and timing.
glossary.vibe coding: Making software by telling an AI what you want and letting it write the code, often without closely checking how it works.
